summary: Repeatedly remove two numbers summing to k; return the maximum number of such operations.
mainInsight: Each number can only pair with k - x. Track unmatched numbers in a hash map: when the complement is waiting, form a pair; otherwise record the number for later.

approaches.name: Sort + two pointers
approaches.summary: Sort; pair ends when the sum equals k, move the side that is too big/small.

approaches.name: Hash map of counts (one pass)
approaches.summary: Look up the complement; consume it if present, else store the current number.
approaches.interviewRelevance: Your approach; the usual optimal-time answer.

personalSolution.notes: Optimal time. Sorting + two pointers trades time for O(1) space.

promptVariants: Which patterns solve Max Number of K-Sum Pairs?
options: Hash map of unmatched values (Two Sum style)
Sliding window over the sorted array with a running sum
Binary search on the answer, checking pair feasibility
Monotonic stack of the unmatched values seen so far
cards.answer: Hash map of unmatched values (Two Sum style)
cards.explanation: Each element needs its complement; a counter map consumes matches greedily.

promptVariants: Why is greedily pairing whenever the complement is available optimal?
Why is the greedy hash-map pairing optimal for Max Number of K-Sum Pairs?
cards.answer: Each number x can only ever pair with k - x, so every x-(k-x) pairing is independent of other values; matching whenever possible cannot reduce the total because the number of pairs for a value pair is min(count(x), count(k-x)).
keyPoints: Pairs = min of the two counts
cards.explanation: That is why one pass suffices.

promptVariants: Time complexity of the hash-map solution: ___
The one-pass hash-map solution to K-Sum Pairs runs in ___ time.
cards.explanation: One pass with O(1) average map operations.

promptVariants: Compare the space of the hash-map and sort + two pointers solutions.
What do you trade when choosing the hash map over sort + two pointers for K-Sum Pairs?
cards.answer: Hash map: O(n) extra space, O(n) time. Sort + two pointers: O(1) extra (besides the sort), O(n log n) time. Choose by what matters more.

promptVariants: Why decrement the stored count and pop at zero, and what changes when nums[i] == complement (e.g. k = 4, value 2)?
How does the counter map handle a value that is its own complement, and why pop at zero?
cards.answer: A matched number is consumed so it cannot be reused: decrement, and pop at zero so `in hmap` stays accurate. When a value equals its own complement the first 2 is stored and the second 2 finds it, forming a pair (the current element is never inserted when it pairs).
keyPoints: Pop at zero keeps membership correct
cards.explanation: defaultdict makes absent keys read as 0 but `in` checks real keys.

promptVariants: What is the answer for [3,1,3,4,3], k = 6?
How are repeated equal values paired?
cards.explanation: Only 3+3 sums to 6 and a single pair of 3s can be formed from the first two available 3s; the third 3 has no partner (1+4 = 5).

incorrectOptionExplanations.2: There are three 3s, enough for one pair only.
